stem: A 71 year old man walks into ED following a fall. He is complaining of neck pain and weakness affecting his upper limbs only. Which of the following spinal cord lesions is most likely:
fact: Central cord syndrome classically causes disproportionately greater motor impairment in the upper extremities after cervical injury.
mnemonic: Central cord: arms affected more than legs.
finding: Clinical neuroanatomy supports the displayed key.

stem: The thalamus surrounds which of the following structures:
fact: The paired thalami form the lateral walls of the third ventricle.
finding: NCBI anatomy supports the displayed key.

stem: The primary auditory cortex is located in which of the following regions:
fact: The primary auditory cortex is located in the temporal lobe, on the transverse temporal gyri.

stem: The primary somatosensory cortex is located in which of the following regions:
fact: The primary somatosensory cortex lies in the postcentral gyrus of the parietal lobe.

stem: Which of the following best describes the position of the frontal lobe:
options: Anterior to the central sulcus and superior to the lateral sulcus
Posterior to the central sulcus and superior to the lateral sulcus
Anterior to the central sulcus and inferior to the lateral sulcus
Posterior to the central sulcus and inferior to the lateral sulcus
fact: The frontal lobe lies anterior to the central sulcus and superior to the lateral sulcus.
mnemonic: Frontal is front and above the lateral sulcus.
finding: Standard cortical surface anatomy supports the displayed key.

stem: Which of the following best describes the position of the parietal lobe:
options: Anterior to the central sulcus and superior to the lateral sulcus
Posterior to the central sulcus and superior to the lateral sulcus
Anterior to the central sulcus and inferior to the lateral sulcus
Posterior to the central sulcus and inferior to the lateral sulcus
fact: The parietal lobe lies posterior to the central sulcus and superior to the lateral sulcus.
mnemonic: Parietal is posterior and superior to the lateral sulcus.
finding: Standard cortical surface anatomy supports the displayed key.

stem: The blood supply to the frontal lobe is primarily supplied by which of the following arteries:
fact: The frontal lobe receives major cortical supply from both the anterior cerebral artery medially and the middle cerebral artery laterally.
finding: The circulation review supports the combined ACA and MCA key; the broad source wording is retained.

stem: The sensation produced by touching the arm with cotton wool during a neurological examination is mediated by which of the following spinal tracts:
fact: Fine touch is conveyed through the posterior-column medial-lemniscus pathway.
mnemonic: Posterior columns carry fine touch, vibration, and proprioception.
finding: NCBI supports the displayed key and source explanation.

stem: A 69 year old patient is brought to ED with acute onset facial weakness on the right side, and difficulty with speech. He is able to respond to questions appropriately by nodding or shaking his head, but his words are jumbled and don't make sense. Which of the following lobes has been affected:
fact: A dominant left frontal lesion involving the primary motor cortex and Broca area can cause right facial weakness with expressive dysphasia.
mnemonic: Broca and face: dominant frontal lobe.
finding: NCBI Broca-area anatomy supports the displayed key.

stem: Which of the following best describes the position of the occipital lobe:
options: Posterior to the central sulcus and inferior to the lateral sulcus
Posterior to the central sulcus and superior to the lateral sulcus
fact: The occipital lobe lies posterior to the parietal and temporal lobes and inferior to the parieto-occipital sulcus in the source description.
mnemonic: Occipital is at the back, below the parieto-occipital sulcus.
finding: NCBI occipital-lobe anatomy supports the displayed key.
